title: Data Organisation, Analysis & Presentation
description: Collecting, organising, presenting, and interpreting data in tables and charts.

questions.q: The data $2,4,4,5,10$ has mode:
questions.explanation: The mode is the value that occurs most often. Here $4$ occurs twice.

questions.q: Find the mean of $3,5,7,9$.
questions.explanation: The sum is $24$ and there are $4$ values, so mean is $6$.

questions.q: Find the median of $1,3,8,10,12$.
questions.explanation: The middle value is $8$.

questions.q: Find the range of $6,9,2,11,5$.
questions.explanation: Range is largest minus smallest: $11-2=9$.

questions.q: A tally mark group of four is usually written as:
questions.explanation: Four tally marks are four separate strokes; the fifth crosses them.

questions.q: Which graph is best for comparing categories?
questions.explanation: A bar chart is used to compare separate categories.

questions.q: Which graph is best for showing change over time?
questions.explanation: A line graph shows trends over time clearly.

questions.q: A pie chart represents a whole as:
questions.explanation: A full pie chart is a full circle, so it has $360^\circ$.

questions.q: In a class of $30$, $12$ learners like football. What pie-chart angle represents football?
A frequency table shows score $5$ has frequency $8$. What does this mean?
questions.explanation: Frequency tells how many times a value occurs.

questions.q: Find the total frequency: $3,5,7,10$.
questions.explanation: Add the frequencies: $3+5+7+10=25$.

questions.q: Scores $1,2,3$ have frequencies $4,5,1$. Find the mean score.
questions.explanation: Weighted total is $1(4)+2(5)+3(1)=17$; total frequency is $10$, so mean is $1.7$.

questions.q: Which is primary data?
options: Data collected by the researcher directly
questions.explanation: Primary data is collected directly for the investigation.

questions.q: Which is secondary data?
questions.explanation: Secondary data has already been collected by another source.

questions.q: A questionnaire is mainly used to collect:
questions.explanation: Questionnaires collect responses from people.

questions.q: Which average is most affected by an extreme value?
questions.explanation: The mean uses every value, so an extreme value can change it strongly.

questions.q: The median is useful because it is:
questions.explanation: The median depends on position, so extreme values affect it less.

questions.q: If a pictogram key says one symbol represents $5$ learners, how many learners do $7$ symbols represent?
questions.explanation: $7\times5=35$ learners.

questions.q: If $20\%$ of a pie chart is shaded, find the angle shaded.
The class interval $10-19$ has class width:
questions.explanation: For whole-number classes, $10-19$ covers $10$ values.

questions.q: The midpoint of the class interval $20-30$ is:
questions.explanation: Midpoint is $(20+30)/2=25$.

questions.q: A histogram is mainly used for:
questions.explanation: Histograms display continuous grouped data.

questions.q: A bar chart should have bars that are:
questions.explanation: For separate categories, bar-chart bars are usually separated.

questions.q: Find the mode of $7,8,8,9,9,9,10$.
questions.explanation: $9$ occurs three times, more than any other value.

questions.q: Find the median of $4,6,8,10$.
questions.explanation: For four values, median is the average of the two middle values: $(6+8)/2=7$.

questions.q: Find the mean of $2,2,6,10$.
questions.explanation: The sum is $20$ and there are $4$ values, so mean is $5$.

questions.q: Which data type is qualitative?
questions.explanation: Eye colour is a category, not a numerical measurement.

questions.q: Which data type is quantitative?
questions.explanation: Number of siblings is numerical.

questions.q: A sample is:
options: a part of the population selected for study
questions.explanation: A sample is a selected part of the population.

questions.q: A population is:
options: all items or people under study
questions.explanation: The population is the full group being studied.

questions.q: Which method is likely to give a biased sample?
questions.explanation: Surveying only friends is unlikely to represent the whole population fairly.

questions.q: The cumulative frequency after frequencies $2,4,6$ is:
questions.explanation: Cumulative frequency adds up to that point: $2+4+6=12$.

questions.q: If the total frequency is $50$, the median position is approximately:
questions.explanation: Median position is $(n+1)/2=(50+1)/2=25.5$.

questions.q: Which display is best for showing parts of a whole?
questions.explanation: A pie chart shows how a whole is divided into parts.

questions.q: A stem-and-leaf plot preserves:
questions.explanation: Stem-and-leaf plots show the individual data values.

questions.q: For data $5,5,6,8,11$, find the range.
questions.explanation: Range is $11-5=6$.

questions.q: If a bar has height $12$ on a frequency chart, the frequency is:
questions.explanation: The height of the bar represents the frequency.

questions.q: Which question is better for collecting numerical data?
questions.explanation: Height is a numerical measurement.

questions.q: A pie-chart sector of $90^\circ$ represents what fraction of the data?
If $8$ out of $40$ learners walk to school, what percentage walk?
